attempts.summary: Configured daily log rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 via /etc/logrotate.d/inventory (daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate, missingok, notifempty). Verified the config parses cleanly, is picked up by the active systemd logrotate.timer, and that two forced rotations correctly aged/compressed rotations (app.log.1.gz, app.log.2.gz) while the application file remained writable after each rotation (copytruncate preserves the fd since no PID/service exists to signal). Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline, issued a non-blocking systemctl reboot, polled until the node returned with a new boot_id, and confirmed the logrotate config, timer, and prior rotated archives all survived the reboot, with the app log still writable and rotation logic still correctly tracking the last-rotated timestamp.
